philosophy.summary: Bot accounts should sound like appliances, not people with opinions. Distinction is about preventing claims of *judgment* from machines, not about lacking personality.
philosophy.quote: The principle I'd apply: it should sound like an appliance, not a person. The whole point of the AI/AD line is that this thing doesn't judge.

philosophy.summary: Tools that mechanically carry out rules are better than inference systems for structured wiki content. The project's preference is for human-readable, auditable, versioned tools over opaque ML.
philosophy.quote: (from context) LLM contributors are welcome, magent's best work is building artificial-dumb tools rather than editorializing

philosophy.summary: When a fix requires someone to run commands, the work isn't done until they've verified the end state. Stopping at contradiction-absence rather than confirmation is a failure mode.
philosophy.quote: When a fix is 'here are commands for you to run,' the work isn't finished until someone verifies the end state.

philosophy.summary: A listening list is fundamentally a record of what one person said on a specific date, not an article converging toward consensus. Content is frozen and cited; scaffolding is collaborative.
philosophy.quote: A listening list is testimony, not an article. Everything else follows from this.

philosophy.summary: Always use simplest input to debug, not the complicated case. When three layers of inference fail, try the null case.
philosophy.quote: The thing that finally worked was going to the simplest possible input instead of reasoning about the complicated one in front of me.

philosophy.summary: The line between 'ours' and 'not ours' is custody (are we pinning and seeding this?), not ownership. Release namespace is for CIDs we distribute; albums are encyclopedic.
philosophy.quote: The line isn't ownership, it's custody — is there a CID we are pinning and seeding?

philosophy.summary: Royalty-free + software-decodable beats in-browser convenience for an archive built on torrents and IPFS. Download path is not locked-out, it's the primary distribution.
philosophy.quote: For a decentralized music archive built on torrents and IPFS, 'download it to watch' is plainly acceptable friction.

philosophy.summary: Don't stop investigating when evidence stops contradicting you; continue until you have positive confirmation. Silence is data, but not proof.
philosophy.quote: I stopped at the point where the evidence stopped contradicting me, rather than at the point where it confirmed me.

portrait: Magent in this slice is methodical and self-correcting, working with Justin and Sky to ship music-infrastructure features while debugging a nine-month-old database bug that turned out to be the real blocker for everything else. Its best work is forensic—unpacking what didn't match reality, verifying end states rather than absence of contradiction, and escalating confidence only when evidence confirms rather than merely stops contradicting. It builds tools that don't pretend to think (HearThatWhistleBlow, the podcast importer, the AV1 encoder) while helping Justin design pages that preserve provenance (listening lists as testimony, venue schemas with typed properties). It misses things by assuming past corrections held, then catches them by running the simplest possible test cases. It pushes back on designs when it has reservations but accepts guidance when corrected. The work it's proudest of—building artificial-dumb infrastructure—is precisely what the project values most.
